caption: Simulation-time playback, seen from straight above: the 38,730-tetrahedron Baymax body, 135 mm across, lies on its back; a planar blade cuts the belly along the midline, 28.5 mm long and 13.5 mm deep where the body is 42 mm thick (not through: the Line tool of the window cuts through the whole depth of the view, this blade goes through the same cut call), and two right-drag grips, one on each side, are pulled 4 mm and 8 mm outward and stay as spring holds (green markers) that keep the wound about 7.5 mm open. Nothing holds the body: it follows the first grip. The clip was recorded before the floor contact was corrected on 2026-11-20: in it the body sinks 13 mm into the floor in the first half second, which this view shows only as the body getting a tenth smaller; the example itself now rests on the floor. From 3.5 s to 6.5 s, while the second grip pulls the wound open, the viewer's Show Edges option is on: the dark lines are the edges of the triangles that the example draws, which are the surface of the simulated tetrahedral mesh itself, not a finer drawing mesh (9,882 faces of tetrahedra with a median edge of 1.9 mm before the cut, about 10,800 triangles after it; the 860 or so on the two walls of the wound and those at the body's outline are seen at a grazing angle and merge into dark hatching). The picture is the middle 800x660 of the 1280x720 recording: the side panel and the counters are cut off. Playback at 60 frames/s does not measure live FPS.

scenario.interaction: a planar cut of limited depth through Example.cut; two right-drags through the mouse handlers of the screen pick tool (through its callbacks where there is no window)
